input.quote: For the purpose of this Agreement, extended payment charges shall be computed at three hundred percent (300%) of the rate described in Subparagraph 7.8 on the day following the date payment on the bill was due.
input.rationale: Subparagraph 7.9 requires a billed Party (including us) to pay "extended payment charges" at 300% of the Subparagraph 7.8 reference (prime) rate, running without time limit until payment. A treble-rate charge is not a compensatory funding cost; it is a penalty payable by us, which fails the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and is not saved by the early-termination-fee fallback, which is inapplicable here. The minimal fix is to strike the 300% multiplier so late payments accrue at the ordinary Subparagraph 7.8 rate. Noted but not separately flagged: Paragraph 23 (p0255-p0256) reclaims capacity and denies reimbursement on default, but only after a payment default persisting roughly three months post-notice and it applies mutually to all Parties (it protects us against other defaulting Parties as well); Paragraph 7.8 charges and the no-credit rule on voluntary termination (p0233) are likewise not Customer-payable penalties.

ops.oldText: three hundred percent (300%) of the rate described in Subparagraph 7.8

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the 300% multiplier so late payments accrue at the compensatory rate in Subparagraph 7.8 rather than a punitive multiple, consistent with our position that no penalties be payable by us. If a margin is needed, we can accept a modest uplift over the 7.8 rate.
proposal.summary: Reduce extended payment charges from 300% of the reference rate to the compensatory reference rate.
